comments:
> Alternative Designs

Should we have a different type for this? Searching for a single match in a fixed set seems to be very different operation from searching for a fixed set match in a sequence.

Another example where this API would be really useful: improving `Uri.Escape` helpers https://github.com/MihaZupan/runtime/commit/a5027e1e21944257669e4bedfaf3d7217cb499f3

A few other cases:
- https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c18e3d9681d3688e4812a09c4549679fea9be0f6/src/libraries/Common/src/System/IO/Archiving.Utils.Windows.cs#L10
- https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/62e87b43207a17caa7b3d3260c1f58f155f5284e/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/src/System/Security/Cryptography/PemEncoding.cs#L200

review_comments: Just curious what the perf looks like if this is made branchless with an `|` instead of an `||`.  I don't know if that's a good tradeoff or not given typical usage, e.g. how likely it is the first check will succeed or fail.
These are all for cases where the condition is never hit
We could also experiment with the sort of optimizations like your (`[x, x + 32)`) in the future here

Interesting... do you think it's worth changing to `|` (at least for 2 & 3) in that case?

Let me rerun these with randomized inputs...

Meh, this can go either way. I'll leave it as-is for now.
